correctness.rationale: The standard \(\ell\)-step derivative is a bijection from a source word to its length-\(\ell\) prefix and derivative tail, and one length-\(\ell\) tandem duplication inserts \(0^\ell\) into that tail. For a fixed nonzero skeleton, distinct source tails are described by zero-run vectors. Two distinct tails share a one-duplication output exactly when one is obtained from the other by transferring \(\ell\) zeros from one zero run to a distinct zero run; the two changed coordinates uniquely determine the common output, proving multiplicity one. For skeleton length \(s\), oriented transfers are counted by \(s(s+1)\binom{n-2\ell}{s}\), so unordered edges contribute half that. Summing over \((q-1)^s\) skeletons and \(q^\ell\) prefixes, then differentiating the binomial theorem twice, gives the closed formula and boundary \(n\le2\ell\). The inspected verifier reconstructs the channel directly over many finite \((q,\ell,n)\) values and matches the formula, but the general proof is combinatorial.

value.rationale: The confusability graph is the natural graph whose independent sets are one-error-correcting codes. An exact edge count for every alphabet size, block length, and source length, together with the exact common-descendant multiplicity, gives structural density information that is reusable for probabilistic, spectral, and extremal studies of these codes. This is an all-parameter invariant, not an arbitrary finite census.
residual_risks: Edge density alone does not determine optimal code size or the degree distribution.

final_claim: For exact one fixed-length tandem duplication on \(\mathbb Z_q^n\), the confusability graph has no edges when \(n\le2\ell\); for \(n\ge2\ell+1\), its edge count is \(\frac{(n-2\ell)(q-1)q^{n-\ell-2}}{2}((q-1)(n-2\ell-1)+2q)\), and every adjacent source pair has exactly one common one-duplication descendant.
limitations: Only exactly one tandem duplication of one fixed length is covered.
The theorem gives total edge count and common-descendant multiplicity, not degree sequence, independence number, optimal code size, mixed lengths, or multiple duplications.
